options: OPTION 1 — 140mm 7.3N dense single leaf + 150mm EPS EWI + thin-coat silicone (continental/Scottish model). STRUCTURE: vertical load from 2 storeys + attic-truss crown roof is fine on 140mm 7.3N (trussed roofs exert little thrust; posi-joist floors give lateral restraint at each level), BUT Approved Document A 'simple rules' expect ~190mm minimum for solid external walls of a 2-storey dwelling — 140mm must go the SE-calculated route (BS EN 1996), typically with buttressing piers at ~3m centres or wind posts on the 8.6m flanks, movement joints at ~6m, and a course of engineering-quality masonry below DPC; budget +£300-500 extra SE design and ~£500 pier/wind-post materials. PART L PATH: 140 dense (R≈0.10) + 150mm grey EPS (λ0.031, R≈4.8) gives U≈0.19; 150mm graphite EPS or 160mm white gets 0.18 — compliant. COST at 130m2: single-leaf shell mats £16-19/m2 block (140mm 7.3N = £1.25-1.75/block, 10/m2, 2026 merchant prices) + £4 mortar/lintels ≈ £2.7k; price-work labour ~£18-20/m2 (heavier 17kg blocks) ≈ £2.5k; piers/SE extras £0.9k → shell ≈ £6.1k vs cavity blockwork £14.3k (saves £8.2k on the leaf). EWI: (a) INCA-member supply+fit 2026 runs £110-180/m2 (EPS installed £145-195/m2 checkatrade; £90-150/m2 low-end guides); on new smooth blockwork with scaffold already in the bill assume bottom-of-market £100-120/m2 → £13-15.6k, and this REPLACES the £6.5k render line. (b) Client-procured route: EWI Pro/EWI Store system materials (150mm EPS £9-14/m2, adhesive £3-4, mesh £1-2, basecoat £4-6, fixings/beads/primer £5-6, silicone topcoat ~£6 at £59ex/25kg) ≈ £38-45/m2 + render-gang fitting labour £45-55/m2 → £85-95/m2 ≈ £11-12.4k, but NO system warranty unless the gang is system-approved. TOTALS: contractor route £6.1k+£14.3k=£20.4k vs cavity £20.8k → saving ≈ £0.4k (a wash). Self-managed route £6.1k+£11.7k=£17.8k → gross saving ≈ £3.0k. INTERFACES: party flank on the boundary CANNOT carry 150mm EPS over the line without neighbour consent under the Party Wall Act — that flank stays masonry-on-the-line regardless (footprint: 140+EWI ≈ 300mm total vs 350mm cavity, marginal internal-area gain elsewhere); window reveals need 20-30mm reveal boards + extended cills (~£40/opening); below-DPC needs XPS perimeter board + starter track/bellcast (~£15/lm ≈ £350); every external fixing needs thermal-break brackets. FIRE: house well under 11m — the Regulation 7(2)/ADB combustibles ban does NOT apply; render-faced EPS systems classify B-s1,d0 as systems, acceptable; only a wall within 1m of the boundary needs the surface class + fire resistance — that is the party flank, which is masonry anyway. Busy-road durability: EPS thin-coat is impact-vulnerable; add HD mesh double-layer to the front ground-storey band +£8-10/m2 (~£300).

OPTION 2 — 215mm solid aircrete (H+H Celcon Solar / Thermalite party-wall laid flat) + thinner EWI. H+H explicitly supports solid-wall construction with 200mm+ blocks and EWI (published U-values to 0.11), and 2.9N at 215mm carries 2 storeys + trussed roof per H+H load tables (SE to confirm; AD A simple rules are satisfied at 215mm — no pier gymnastics). Part L: 215 Solar (λ0.11, R1.95) + 110-120mm EPS → U 0.17-0.18. BUT THE ARITHMETIC KILLS IT: 215mm Solar = £53.60/m2 +VAT mats (2026 merchant price) ≈ £7.0k over 130m2, + laying labour £20-24/m2 (big heavy units or thin-joint premium) ≈ £2.9k → shell £9.9k, + 110mm EWI fitted ~£105/m2 = £13.7k → total £23.6k vs cavity £20.8k = £2.8k WORSE. The thermal block premium plus almost-undiminished EWI cost means you pay twice for insulation. KILL.

OPTION 3 — 140mm single leaf + insulated stud liner INSIDE (IWI) instead of EWI. Cost looks tempting: shell £6.1k + external mesh-basecoat silicone render still required £6.5k + IWI incremental over the drylining already in fit-out (89mm stud, 90mm Frametherm, VCL) ~£35-45/m2 ≈ £5.0k → £17.6k, apparent saving £3.2k. CONDENSATION VERDICT: fails. DESNZ/BEIS IWI best-practice research: installing IWI 'always led to an increased moisture risk'; dense blockwork behind a silicone-rendered face with warm-side insulation puts the dew point inside cold masonry, demanding an intelligent vapour-control membrane, sealed service void and flawless workmanship — on a NEW build there is zero reason to accept retrofit-grade moisture risk. Also loses ~0.1m around ~14m of external wall per floor x 3 floors ≈ 4m2+ of floor area, worth £8-12k at B14 values — more than the entire saving. KILL.

OPTION 6a — masonry GF + timber-frame first floor/attic with render carrier board (Bluclad/Cempanel) + thin-coat. 2026 wall-level costs: stick-built timber frame walls £1,000-1,200/m2-of-plan vs cavity blockwork £800-1,000 (BestBuilders); at elevation level 140mm stud + Frametherm + OSB + breather + carrier board (£25-30/m2 board alone) + thin-coat render lands ~£150-170/m2 vs cavity walls+render ~£160/m2 — a wash at best, with a live differential-movement crack line in the render at the masonry/frame junction, party-flank fire build-up still needing masonry, and nothing gained since cheapness beats speed here. KILL for savings; keep only if programme ever mattered.

OPTION 6b — 215mm ('9-inch') commons solid brick: 120 bricks/m2 x £0.55-0.65 = £66-78/m2 materials + price-work labour (£700/1000 domestic rate ≈ £84/m2 at 120/m2) → £150+/m2 before any insulation, then still needs full EWI. Two to three times the blockwork lines. KILL. OPTION 6c — reclaimed/recycled block: no UKCA/CE declaration of conformity, so SE and Building Control will not accept it loadbearing without testing; supply is negligible. KILL.
singleLeaf.lender_verdict: Mostly benign but not zero-risk, and it is the one option that carries ANY resale tail-risk. (1) The property overall remains standard construction — a rendered extension on a 1930s cavity/solid-brick house does not re-classify the house, and valuers rarely open up an extension's build-up; the exposure is via the Building Control completion certificate and seller's pack at resale. (2) 'Single skin' is a recognised lender red flag: several lenders exclude single-skin areas from valuation or demand a structural report (Strive Mortgages, OnlineMoneyAdvisor, Charcol, MSE forum cases of valuations failing on single-skin walls) — but that literature is about 102mm half-brick lean-tos; a 140mm engineered leaf with a BBA-certified EWI system and a completion certificate sits in a grey zone a minority of surveyors could still label 'single skin'. 215mm solid masonry is unambiguously traditional/standard construction (millions of pre-1919 solid-wall houses). (3) EWI itself: houses under 11m need no EWS1 and the combustibles ban does not apply; lenders accept BBA/Kiwa-certified EWI systems, and INCA-member installation with a system warranty is what a surveyor looks for. NET: cavity = zero questions ever; 140mm+EWI = small but real chance of a picky valuer or conveyancer raising 'single-skin extension' at resale, mitigable with BBA system certificate + installer warranty + BC completion cert kept on file.
singleLeaf.net_saving_vs_cavity: Lines in play (verified cavity bill, ~130m2 gross wall): blockwork both skins £14.3k + render £6.5k = £20.8k (ties/DriTherm inside the blockwork line). BEST CHEAPER CASE (Option 1, 140mm leaf + self-procured EWI at £85-95/m2 fitted): £6.1k shell + £11.7k EWI = £17.8k → gross saving £3.0k; deduct extra SE design £0.4k, below-DPC/reveal/cill sundries £0.6k, front impact-mesh band £0.3k → NET SAVING ≈ £1.7-2.3k, i.e. about 1% of the £195-210k project — and it evaporates entirely (≈£0.4k, a wash) if a warranty-backed INCA contractor prices the EWI at the normal £100-120/m2. Option 2 (215 aircrete) is £2.8k WORSE; Option 3 (IWI) 'saves' £3.2k but destroys £8-12k of floor-area value plus moisture risk; timber-frame hybrid and 9-inch brick are a wash or worse. There is no wall system that beats cavity by more than ~£2k on this envelope.
singleLeaf.recommendation: Stay with the winning price-work cavity spec. The honest maximum saving from any single-leaf/solid-wall route is ~£2k (~1%) and only in the self-managed-EWI variant that sacrifices the system warranty; the contractor-priced variant saves nothing. Against that ~£2k the single-leaf route buys: an AD-A departure needing SE-calculated 140mm with piers (or a step up to 190/215mm that erases the saving), a party-flank boundary where EWI cannot overhang anyway, impact-vulnerable EPS render on a busy-road frontage, reveal/DPC/fixing detailing that a price-work masonry gang will fumble on their first EWI job, and the only lender/'single-skin' resale tail-risk of any option. Cavity masonry at £195-210k stands. If the client wants one cheap lever that actually moves the total, it is procurement (client-supplied materials accounts, second quotes on piles and trusses), not the wall build-up. Only revisit single-leaf if a warranty-backed INCA installer quotes ≤£85/m2 fitted for 150mm EPS — get one quote to confirm the kill, then close the question.

line_savings: PILES+BEAMS: current 18,000; achievable 14,000-14,500. How: 2026 mini-piling for a domestic extension benchmarks at 4.5k-8k plus beams (Checkatrade/PropertyWorkshop; screw piles GBP 100-200/lm, mini-piles GBP 75-150/lm). If the borehole finds firm Birmingham mudstone/marl at modest depth, have the SE respace piles from ~2.0m to 2.5-3.0m centres on deeper beams (perimeter ~29m: drops 4-6 piles at ~GBP 450-600/pile installed = 2,000-3,000) and restrict screw piles to the 700mm tree's RPA only, cheaper augered mini-piles elsewhere in the piled zone (saves ~1,000-1,500). Do NOT switch to driven piles: vibration risk against the party flank garage and PWA claims outweigh the ~10% saving. Risk: saving is 100% borehole-conditional; bad ground claws it all back.

BEAM-AND-BLOCK FLOOR: current 5,000; achievable 5,000 (hold). How: 51.6m2 at the 2026 benchmark GBP 65-110/m2 installed means the line is already at ~GBP 97/m2 - fair. Raft-on-piles is NOT cheaper here (raft GBP 150-300/m2 2026, plus heave void formers in the RPA); beam-and-block spans the heave zone natively. Risk: none - do not touch this line.

DEMO + SKIPS/PLANT: current 9,000 combined; achievable 8,000. How: Birmingham 8yd skips run GBP 280-340 in 2026; a 16t grab load for the demo arisings and pile spoil replaces 3-4 skips (saves ~500-800). Volumetric mixer for ground beams/oversite (~10m3 at GBP 120-150/m3) kills part-load waste charges vs drum ready-mix (saves ~200-300). Risk: low; grab needs kerbside slot on a busy road - book early-morning lifts.

BLOCKWORK: current 14,300; achievable 14,000 (essentially hold). How: 2026 Midlands price-work confirms GBP 17.50-20/m2 for 100mm blockwork and brickie day rates GBP 200-300 - the 7.2k labour line is already price-work-lean. Cavity masonry remains the winner: no cheaper compliant wall exists at this spec (timber frame saves nothing once the render carrier board and fire detailing at the party flank are priced). Risk: none.

STEELS 5,500 / POSI-JOISTS 4,800: achievable 5,200 / 4,800. How: steels - get 3 fabricator quotes ex-works and pay a labour-only gang to erect (typical 5-8% saving ~300); posi line already competitive vs 2026 joist pricing. Risk: minimal.

ROOF - TRUSSES+CARPENTRY: current 12,000 (7.5k trusses + 4.5k erect); achievable 11,000. How: attic trusses at GBP 100-170/unit supply (2026) means ~7.5k is mid-market - tender to 3 Midlands fabricators (Donaldson, Harlow, local) for ~700-1,000 off. A cut roof LOSES: 2 carpenters x 3-4 weeks at Birmingham GBP 220-330/day = 9k-13k labour plus 3-4k loose timber, before SE design. SIPs/TRADA room-in-roof panels LOSE at ~GBP 197/m2 before cladding. No-crane constraint: hiab off-load + hand-set is fine for attic trusses; price 1 day telehandler in plant. Risk: low.

ROOF - TILES: current 5,300; achievable 4,000-4,300. How: Marley Ashmore (double-plain interlocking, ~19/m2 coverage) costs roughly double a standard large-format concrete interlocking (~10/m2 coverage) per m2 of roof; on ~100m2 of pitched skirt that's ~1,000-1,500 supply saving, more via overstock pallet dealers (Roofing Outlet etc.). 2026 concrete-tile benchmark GBP 45-65/m2 fitted supports the lower figure. Risk: planning drawings may condition the tile appearance - needs a non-material amendment check before ordering; do not swap without it.

ROOF - FLAT CENTRE: current 2,500 EPDM; achievable 1,400-1,600. How: buy the EPDM as a supply-only kit (~GBP 25-35/m2 materials for ~20-25m2 = 700-850) and pay a roofer labour-only 1-2 days (~500-600). Keep EPDM: felt saves only ~600 more but halves the life over a habitable loft; GRP (GBP 80-150/m2 2026) is dearer and cracks on big deflecting decks. Risk: low - one-piece membrane, hidden detail.

ROOF - LEAD/FASCIA: current 2,200; achievable 1,800. How: composite flashing (Ubiflex/LeadX) instead of Code 4 lead saves ~300-400 and removes theft risk on a busy road. Risk: minimal; BC accepts BBA-certified substitutes.

WINDOWS: current 8,000; achievable 6,500. How: 2026 supply-only trade uPVC runs GBP 200-450/frame vs 500-800 installed; self-supply ~8 frames + French doors (~4,500-5,000) and pay a labour-only fitter (~1,200-1,500). Risk: measure errors are yours - pay the fitter to survey; FENSA route gone so BC inspects (already in fees).

RENDER: current 6,500; achievable 5,800-6,000. How: self-supply the silicone system (basecoat ~3.50/m2 + mesh ~1.50 + primer + topcoat = ~GBP 12-15/m2 materials) and use a sub-threshold price-work render gang at GBP 30-40/m2 labour on ~110m2 = ~4,700-5,500 all-in; 2026 supply-and-fit benchmark is GBP 55-100/m2 so the 6.5k line was already keen - take the last 500-700 only via labour-only + own materials. Risk: mesh-basecoat needs a continuous boarded scaffold lift - do not economise the scaffold under the renderers.

SCAFFOLD: current 5,500; achievable 4,500. How: 2026 single-elevation scaffold is GBP 650-1,100 and standard quotes include 6-8 weeks free hire; tender 3 local firms, negotiate 12-week free hire aligned to blockwork-roof-render sequence, drop the front elevation if untouched. Tower-per-elevation does NOT work for mesh-basecoat render or truss erection. Risk: programme slip beyond free hire adds GBP 10-25/week/elevation - sequencing is the PM's job.

SE/BC/PARTY-WALL: current 6,000; achievable 4,500. How: 2026 BC extension fees ~GBP 600-1,000 all-in (plans 250-550 + inspections 330-470) - get LA and two registered-approver quotes; SE calc package 1,500-2,000 (piles+steels+3-storey justifies top of the 500-1,200 band); party wall - hand-deliver notices with drawings and a written schedule of condition and seek neighbour CONSENT (GBP 0) instead of defaulting to a surveyor award (1,200+). Risk: neighbour dissent restores the 1,200-1,500; budget it in contingency, not the plan.

FIT-OUT - DRYLINING: current 10,000; achievable 8,000-8,500. How: 2026 price-work: tacking GBP 8-14/m2, skim 8-15/m2, boards 3-8/m2; on ~450-500m2 a tack-and-skim gang lands 8.5-10k, so compress by self-supplying boards from seconds channels (Seconds & Co insulated boards; standard 12.5mm seconds ~40-50% off) and tape-and-joint instead of skim in the loft storey. Risk: seconds supply is lumpy - buy the whole quantity when a batch appears.

FIT-OUT - ELECTRICS: current 8,000; achievable 6,000-6,500. How: 2026 per-point rate GBP 80-150 includes materials/margin; a labour-only registered spark on price-work with client-supplied accessories and cable does ~65 points at 70-90/point = 4,500-6,000 + CU and certification. The Grade D1/LD2 interlinked alarm set stays in scope. Risk: must remain a Part P registered installer for self-certification - never split certification from installation.

FIT-OUT - PLUMBING: current 7,000; achievable 5,500. How: labour-only plumber at GBP 280-480/day (2026), 10-13 days for CH extension + 2 wet rooms = 3,500-5,000; client supplies boiler/rads/pipe on own trade account (~1,200-1,500). Risk: unvented/gas work needs Gas Safe - keep boiler connection as a priced package.

FIT-OUT - BATHROOMS: current 5,500; achievable 4,500. How: full install benchmark GBP 1,500-4,500 (2026); budget bundle suites at 600-900/room + tile seconds + the labour-only plumber above; land 2 rooms at ~2,200 each including tiling. Risk: cheap sanitaryware quality - stick to trade brands' entry ranges (Roca/Vitra).

FIT-OUT - LOFT STAIRS: current 3,500; achievable 2,300-2,500. How: standard softwood straight flight supplied and fitted GBP 800-1,500 low-end / 1,500-3,000 typical (2026); the opening is already framed in the posi-joist design so buy a made-to-measure softwood flight (~700-900 supply) + 2 days carpenter. Risk: winder flights jump to 2,000-4,000 - keep the straight flight in the layout.

FIT-OUT - FIRE PACKAGE: current 3,000; achievable 2,300-2,500. How: FD30 doors GBP 150-300 each supply, from ~180 fitted (2026); ~6-7 doors + LD2 alarms (alarms priced within electrics) = 1,800-2,300; use FD30 leaves in new linings, doorsets only where frames are new. Scope stays NON-NEGOTIABLE - three-storey protected stair, FD30/FD20 enclosure, mains interlinked alarms every level. Risk: none tolerable - this line compresses on price only, never scope.

FIT-OUT - DOORS/JOINERY 5,000 to 4,000 (ex-display/seconds doors, bulk MDF); ROOFLIGHTS 2,500 to 1,800 (Dakea/RoofLITE+/Keylite at 10-20%+ under Velux, ~250-350/unit supply); FLOORING 3,000 to 2,500 (trade LVT/carpet deals); DECORATION 4,000 to 3,200 (price-work decorator - client is not hands-on so cannot be zeroed); GF INSULATION+SCREED 3,500 hold; SUNDRIES/INSURANCE 3,500 to 3,100 (self-build site insurance market rate GBP 600-1,200, Protek from ~228 base - shop the renewal). Combined saving ~2,900. Risk: budget rooflight flashing compatibility - buy flashings same-brand.

CONTINGENCY: current 17,000 (~9%); achievable 15,000 IF the borehole is clean and the neighbour consents - the two biggest unknowns die early. Risk: do not cut below ~8.5% on a piled three-storey party-wall job; this is the last line to spend, not the first to delete.
billAttack.vat_limit: Honest limit: VAT drag compresses from ~12,000 to ~8,000-8,500, no further. Facts (2026/27): registration threshold frozen at GBP 90,000 (deregistration 88,000); a domestic extension is STANDARD-RATED - no 5% empty-home relief (house occupied), no DIY VAT431 reclaim (extensions excluded), no zero-rating. What works: (1) every labour package (brickies, carpenters, roof tilers, render gang, drylining, spark, plumber, decorator, stair fitter) placed with genuinely sub-threshold sole traders = 0% VAT on ~55-65k of labour, saving the ~11-13k a VAT-registered main contractor would add; (2) client self-supplies ALL materials on own merchant accounts, so 20% is paid only on net merchant cost, never on a builder's marked-up materials. What cannot be avoided: 20% inside piling (~2,400), truss supply (~1,100), scaffold (~750), skips/grab/plant (~600), beam-and-block supply, render system materials, insulation/boards, windows supply, merchant materials generally (~55-60k of materials = ~9-10k VAT embedded, most already inside the line prices) - hence the residual ~8k drag. Hard warnings: 'cash, no VAT' from a registered trade is fraud - walk away; and do not let one builder artificially split into two entities to stay under 90k (HMRC disaggregation rules); hiring genuinely independent trades is entirely legal.
billAttack.phasing: Loft-shell phasing verdict: smaller than hoped, because of Part B. With a FIXED STAIRCASE installed, building control treats the loft as a third storey regardless of a 'non-habitable storage' label (LABC/ADB guidance, MyBuilder/DIYnot BC consensus) - so the protected stairway enclosure, FD30/FD20 doors on rooms off the stair on ALL floors, mains interlinked LD2 alarms including the loft level, and the escape strategy must ALL be built NOW; the roof insulation (0.15) must also go in now because Part L completion applies to the finished thermal envelope and the tiles/render seal it. Genuinely deferrable: loft drylining/skim (~3.5k), loft bathroom (~2.5k incl plumbing share), loft flooring/decoration (~1.3k), loft second-fix electrics beyond alarms (~0.8k), loft doors/trim (~0.7k) = ~8,500-9,500 deferred. Cost NOW with loft as boarded, insulated, alarmed, fire-doored shell with stairs: roughly 167,000-171,000. Finishing later: the deferred ~9k becomes ~11,000-11,500 (second mobilisation, stair-route protection/making-good, 3-4%/yr inflation, possibly a fresh BC application if the completion certificate described the loft as storage) - i.e. phasing COSTS about 2,000-2,500 extra overall in exchange for deferring ~9k of cash. Sequencing rule unchanged: CIL Form 9 residential-extension exemption claimed AND acknowledged, then Form 6 commencement notice acknowledged, BEFORE any material start - miss it and the surcharge is the lower of 20% of notional CIL or 2,500, plus loss of instalments.
billAttack.honest_floor_full: Full envelope finished floor: GBP 175,000-180,000 (central ~178,000) versus the verified 195,000-210,000 - built from ~23-25k of identified line savings discounted to the ~18-19k that realistically lands, with contingency held at 15k. Risk in one line: this floor requires a clean borehole, a consenting party-wall neighbour, planning tolerance on the tile swap, and a PM who tenders every package three ways and self-supplies all materials - each condition that fails claws back 1,500-4,500.
billAttack.honest_floor_phased: Loft-shell phased floor: GBP 167,000-171,000 spent now (central ~169,000), with ~11,000-11,500 more later to finish the loft - total ~180,000-182,000, i.e. phasing buys ~9k of cash-flow deferral at a ~2,000-2,500 premium. Risk in one line: the fixed staircase makes full three-storey fire compliance (protected stair, FD30 doors, LD2 alarms, roof insulation) unavoidable NOW, so the deferral is finishes-only - and a completion certificate issued with the loft as 'storage' may trigger a second building-control application when it is finished as habitable.

killed_double_counts: KILLED: claiming the blockwork saving (14.3k to ~11k for single leaf) AND keeping the 6.5k render line as a separate saving - EWI REPLACES the render line at 90-140 GBP/m2; priced honestly the wall+finish system goes from 20.8k (cavity+render) to 24.6-28k (215 block+EWI), a 4-7k LOSS, not a gain.

KILLED: deleting DriTherm 32 (~2k) as a standalone saving on top of the wall-line saving - the cavity insulation is already inside the 7.1k materials figure within the 14.3k line; it cannot be subtracted twice.

KILLED: 'go labour-only to save VAT' on blockwork/carpentry - those lines (7.2k bricklaying labour, 4.5k roof carpentry) are already priced as VAT-unregistered price-work gangs, and the 12k VAT-drag line already models exactly that split; no incremental saving exists.

KILLED: loft-shell phasing counted alongside a separate 'delete fire package 3k' cut - the fire-package deferral IS the shell phasing (and ~0.5k of interlinked alarms must stay); counting both takes the same 3k twice.

KILLED: rooflight deferral (2.5k) claimed together with a scaffold reduction - scaffold (5.5k) is needed for the crown roof regardless, and deferring rooflights means paying for access twice later; rooflights go in with the roof, no saving.
KILLED: applying a 'thin-joint 30% labour saving' to the whole 14.3k wall line - labour is only 7.2k of it, so the claim was overstated roughly 2x even before feasibility.
regs_checks: Single-leaf feasibility at 2.5 storeys: possible only as 215mm solid blockwork (or SE-designed 190/140 with piers) - 100mm single skin fails slenderness for three masonry storeys. 215mm costs ~85-95 GBP/m2 laid, saving only ~3k vs both cavity skins before EWI is added.

EWI fire near boundary: AD B requires B-s3,d2 or better on external surfaces within 1m of the relevant boundary; quality EPS thin-coat systems CAN achieve B-s3,d2, so fire class alone does not bar EPS - but the party flank against the neighbour's garage cannot take EWI at all (a ~170mm system oversails the boundary, and the Party Wall Act grants no right to oversail with insulation), forcing a hybrid wall build-up; many BC officers and BBA certs push mineral wool (100-170 GBP/m2) near boundaries anyway, erasing the EPS price edge.

Loft-shell legal position: fit a fixed stair and the loft is a storey - full three-storey package (protected stairway to final exit, FD30/FD20 doors, mains interlinked alarms) becomes non-negotiable, as bid. Hatch-only, non-habitable shell keeps the dwelling at 2 storeys for Part B: stair, fire-door set and loft fit-out can be lawfully deferred, but you must still provide an FD30-rated hatch, mains interlinked smoke/heat alarms to the extended 2-storey layout, escape windows at first floor, and full Part L roof insulation (U 0.15) now because the roof is the thermal envelope from day one. Later conversion needs a second Building Regs application.

CIL: Form 6 commencement notice before any start (Form 9 sequencing as flagged) is unaffected by phasing; the loft floorspace is created and counted in phase 1, so the later fit-out adds no new CIL - keep both phases inside the one planning permission.
Part L: swap must still hit walls 0.18 - 215mm dense block needs ~140-150mm EWI or the aircrete equivalent, which is exactly the 150mm system priced; no thinner-cheaper route exists.
three_numbers: (a) Cavity as-bid: 195,000 GBP (bill sums 193.6k; band 195-210k). Risk: the pending borehole is the one live variable - a bad result moves the 18k piles/beams line, not the walls.

(b) Cheapest defensible wall swap (215mm single leaf + EPS EWI where lawful, hybrid detail at party flank): ~199,000-205,000 GBP - i.e. 4-10k MORE than cavity. Risk: EWI cannot oversail the party boundary at the garage flank, mineral-wool substitution near boundaries kills the EPS price, and lenders/insurers resist single-skin rendered masonry.

(c) Cavity + hatch-only loft-shell phasing: ~183,000 GBP phase-1 cash (defer stairs 3.5k, ~2.5k of fire package, ~4.5k loft drylining/electrics/flooring/decoration, plus ~2.2k pro-rata contingency and VAT drag; keep rooflights and full roof insulation in phase 1). Risk: this is a deferral, not a saving - finishing later costs the ~12k deferred plus ~2-3k remobilisation, and until then the loft is legally storage only.
verdict.cavity_verdict: No - abandoning cavity is not worth it. At verified 2026 prices the cavity wall+render system (~20.8k, ~160 GBP/m2 finished) is CHEAPER than any compliant single-leaf+EWI alternative (24.6-28k), because EWI at 90-140 GBP/m2 replaces the 6.5k render line at a higher rate while the 215mm single leaf saves only ~3k of blockwork - and the party-flank boundary makes full EWI physically impossible anyway. Cavity as-bid stands as the winning method; timber frame and ICF were not cheaper either. The only real lever left is phasing, not the wall build-up.
verdict.true_floor_statement: The true floor for the finished house is the cavity scheme as-bid at ~195,000 GBP; the true floor for phase-1 cash outlay is ~183,000 GBP by leaving the loft as a hatch-access non-habitable shell (stair, fire-door package and loft fit-out deferred), accepting that completing it later costs ~14-15k, i.e. total-project cost never drops below ~195k - the wall swap raises it, and only phasing lowers what is spent now.
verified_facts: EWI installed cost UK 2026: EPS system with render 90-120 GBP/m2, mineral wool 100-170 GBP/m2, full systems averaging ~150-175 GBP/m2 at the quality end (Checkatrade, MyBuilder, Eco Insulation 2026 cost guides).

215mm dense blockwork 2025/26: blocks ~4.00-5.50 GBP each, block-laying labour 25-45 GBP/m2 above DPC; finished masonry wall benchmarks ~150-180 GBP/m2 incl. builder margin (Checkatrade block calculator, Build It cost guide) - confirming the verified 14.3k cavity line is already keen at ~100-110 GBP/m2 for both skins.

AD B boundary rule: external wall surfaces within 1m of the relevant boundary must be class B-s3,d2 or better; quality EPS EWI systems are certified to at least B-s3,d2 (INCA, EWI Pro) - so the swap fails on boundary oversail and economics, not on fire class per se.

Fire regs on the third storey: a habitable loft accessed by a fixed stair requires a protected stairway to the final exit with FD30/FD20 doors throughout; a non-habitable hatch-only loft does not, needing only a fire-rated (FD30) hatch and standard 2-storey alarm provision (Homebuilding, Aldridge Security, Trade Access Panels guides) - which is what makes shell phasing lawful.
